chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

An uncircumcised man should not lead the people in salat (prayer), even if he is the most proficient of them in reciting the Qur'an, because he has neglected one of the greatest parts of the sunnah (prophetic tradition). His testimony is not accepted, and salat (prayer) is not performed over him, unless he left that out of fear for his life.

key_terms.لِلْقُرْآنِ: for the Qur'an, meaning in recitation proficiency
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads as Imam in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: funeral salat (prayer) is performed over him

ai.seo_question: Can an uncircumcised man lead congregational salat (prayer) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the uncircumcised man and states that he is not to lead the congregation in salat (prayer), even if he is the most skilled in Qur'an recitation. It also states legal consequences regarding the acceptance of testimony and funeral salat (prayer), while exempting the case of one who left circumcision out of fear for his life.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "An uncircumcised man (al-aghlaf) should not lead the people in prayer, even if he is the most proficient in reciting the Qur'an among them, because he has neglected one of the greatest aspects of the Sunnah. His testimony is not accepted, and prayers are not performed over him unless he left it (circumcision) out of fear for his life."
